nodes.title: the Quilpon signature
nodes.statement: The Quilpon system concerns objects called lumpons. There are exactly 6 of them: glimtez, glimkorr, nakkorr, duthwren, kaka, mornhob. One operation is written -. One relation is written >-, read as "precedes".

nodes.title: the Quilpon combination tables
nodes.statement: The value of x - y for every pair of lumpons is fixed by the table of the first operation. The pairs standing in the >- relation are listed in full.

nodes.title: closure under the first operation
nodes.statement: For all lumpons x and y, x - y is again a lumpon.

nodes.title: association of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all lumpons x, y, z: (x - y) - z = x - (y - z).

nodes.title: commutation of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all lumpons x and y: x - y = y - x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a lumpon glimtez with glimtez - x = x - glimtez = x for every x.

nodes.title: reversal under the first operation
nodes.statement: For every lumpon x there is a lumpon y with x - y = y - x = glimtez.

nodes.title: cancellation in the first operation
nodes.statement: For all lumpons x, y, z: if x - y = x - z then y = z.

nodes.title: reflexivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For every lumpon x: x >- x.

nodes.title: antisymmetry of the relation
nodes.statement: For all lumpons x and y: if x >- y and y >- x then x = y.

nodes.title: transitivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For all lumpons x, y, z: if x >- y and y >- z then x >- z.

nodes.title: comparability of every pair
nodes.statement: For all lumpons x and y, at least one of x >- y and y >- x holds.

nodes.title: the system does not have self combination under the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every lumpon x: x - x = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = glimkorr, value = nakkorr, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have an absorbing object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is no lumpon z with z - x = x - z = z for every lumpon x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case reason = no absorbing element, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have agreement of the relation with the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all lumpons x, y, z: if x >- y then (z - x) >- (z - y) and (x - z) >- (y - z).

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = glimtez, y = glimkorr, z = mornhob, side = left, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: pontez lumpons
nodes.statement: A lumpon x is called pontez when x - x = x.

nodes.title: lumpons that vorhurn
nodes.statement: Two lumpons x and y are said to vorhurn when x - y = y - x.

nodes.title: lumvex collections
nodes.statement: A collection S of lumpons is lumvex when x - y belongs to S for every pair x, y drawn from S.

nodes.title: the yukglim of a lumpon
nodes.statement: The yukglim of a lumpon x is the collection of lumpons y for which x >- y holds.

nodes.title: the tuka
nodes.statement: The lumpon glimtez is called the tuka of the system. It is the unique lumpon that leaves every lumpon unchanged under -.

nodes.title: the glimfex
nodes.statement: The glimfex of the system is the collection of lumpons that vorhurn with every lumpon.

nodes.title: the opalkeld
nodes.statement: The opalkeld is the collection of all pontez lumpons.

nodes.title: the umbquil of a lumpon
nodes.statement: The umbquil of a lumpon x, written [x], is the smallest lumvex collection that contains x.

nodes.title: a aztlum
nodes.statement: A lumpon f is a aztlum when f >- y holds for every lumpon y, that is, when the yukglim of f is the whole system.

nodes.title: iskjen lumpons
nodes.statement: A lumpon x is iskjen when x - x equals the tuka.

nodes.title: the zamduth of a lumpon
nodes.statement: A zamduth of a lumpon x is a lumpon y with x - y = y - x = glimtez.

nodes.title: the duthovi of a lumpon
nodes.statement: The duthovi of a lumpon x is the number of lumpons in its umbquil [x].

nodes.title: the vashopal
nodes.statement: The vashopal of the system is the collection of lumpons whose duthovi is largest.

nodes.title: cloka pairs
nodes.statement: Two distinct lumpons x and y form a cloka pair when x >- y and y >- x both hold, that is, when each lies in the yukglim of the other.

nodes.title: the tuka is the only one of its kind
nodes.statement: There is exactly one lumpon e with e - x = x - e = x for every lumpon x.

verification.domain: every object paired with every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose e and f both leave every lumpon unchanged.
Then e - f = f, reading e as neutral on the left.
And e - f = e, reading f as neutral on the right.
So e = f, and the two suppositions describe the same object.

nodes.title: the tuka lies in the glimfex
nodes.statement: The tuka vorhurns with every lumpon.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let e be the tuka and x any lumpon.
Then e - x = x and x - e = x.
So e - x = x - e, which is what it means to vorhurn.
Since x was arbitrary, e belongs to the glimfex.

nodes.title: a lumpon has only one zamduth
nodes.statement: For every lumpon x there is exactly one zamduth of x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y and z both be partners of x.
Then y = y - (x - z) = (y - x) - z.
Both bracketed products collapse to the neutral object.
So y = z.

nodes.title: a iskjen lumpon is its own zamduth
nodes.statement: If x - x is the tuka then the zamduth of x is x itself.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x be iskjen, so x - x is the tuka.
That is exactly the condition for x to be a partner of x.
Partners are unique, so no other object can be one.

nodes.title: the glimfex is lumvex
nodes.statement: If x and y both vorhurn with every lumpon, then so does x - y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y lie in the glimfex and let z be any lumpon.
Then (x - y) - z = x - (y - z).
Move z past y, then past x, using that each vorhurns with everything.
So x - y vorhurns with z, and the glimfex is lumvex.

nodes.title: the umbquil of a lumpon is lumvex
nodes.statement: For every lumpon x, the collection [x] is lumvex.

verification.domain: every object, then every pair inside its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is built by taking x and closing under -.
Closing under an operation is exactly the sealing condition.
The carrier is finite, so the closure stops after finitely many rounds.

nodes.title: the umbquil is contained in every lumvex collection
nodes.statement: If S is lumvex and contains x, then S contains all of [x].

verification.domain: every sealed collection against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every member of [x] is reached from x by finitely many applications of the operation.
A sealed S containing x is closed under each of those applications.
So each member of [x] is in S, by induction on the number of applications.

nodes.title: a lumpon is pontez exactly when its duthovi is one
nodes.statement: x - x = x holds if and only if [x] contains x alone.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: If x - x = x then {x} is already closed under -.
So [x] = {x} and the duthovi is one.
Conversely a span of one object must contain x - x, which is then x.

nodes.title: the duthovi divides the number of lumpons
nodes.statement: For every lumpon x, the duthovi of x divides 6.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is a lumvex collection.
Its size is the duthovi of x.
The claim is that this size always divides 6.

nodes.title: the umbquil of a glimfex lumpon stays in the glimfex
nodes.statement: If x lies in the glimfex then every lumpon of [x] lies in the glimfex.

verification.domain: every object of the core, then its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The glimfex is lumvex.
[x] is the smallest lumvex collection containing x.
A smallest such collection sits inside any other, and the glimfex is one.

nodes.title: the opalkeld is lumvex
nodes.statement: If x and y are both pontez then so is x - y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the ridge
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y be pontez.
The claim asks whether (x - y) - (x - y) returns x - y.
Whether it does is settled by running the operation table on every such pair.

nodes.title: combining on the left never merges two lumpons
nodes.statement: For every lumpon a, the assignment x to a - x sends distinct lumpons to distinct lumpons.

verification.domain: every object translated by every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose a - x = a - y.
Cancellation on the left gives x = y.
So the assignment is injective, and being injective on a finite carrier it is onto.

nodes.title: yukglims are nested along the relation
nodes.statement: If y lies in the yukglim of x, then the yukglim of y is contained in the yukglim of x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y satisfy x >- y and let z satisfy y >- z.
Transitivity gives x >- z.
So every member of the yukglim of y is a member of that of x.

nodes.title: there is at most one aztlum
nodes.statement: No two distinct lumpons can both be aztlums.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let f and h both be floors.
Then f >- h, since h is any object, and h >- f likewise.
Antisymmetry forces f = h.

nodes.title: the system has a aztlum
nodes.statement: Some lumpon aztlums the whole system.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every pair is comparable, so the relation orders the objects into a line.
The claim is that the line has a bottom.
The carrier is finite, so the search over candidates terminates.

nodes.title: no cloka pairs exist
nodes.statement: No two distinct lumpons lie in each other's yukglim.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose x and y form a tight pair.
Antisymmetry then identifies x with y.
So a tight pair of distinct objects cannot arise.

nodes.title: every lumpon lies in the glimfex
nodes.statement: Every pair of lumpons vorhurns.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The glimfex is defined by vorhurning with everything.
The claim is that x - y = y - x for every pair.
That is settled by scanning the table for a pair that disagrees.

nodes.title: where every lumpon is pontez breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: x - x = x for every lumpon x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = glimkorr, value = nakkorr, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: some lumpon reaches every other
nodes.statement: There is a lumpon whose umbquil is the whole system.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Compute [x] for each lumpon in turn.
The claim is that some duthovi equals 6.
The search runs over finitely many objects, so it settles.

nodes.title: where the relation reads the same in both directions breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: If x >- y then y >- x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = glimtez, y = glimkorr, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where the tuka swallows everything breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: e - x equals the tuka for every lumpon x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case anchor = glimtez, x = glimkorr, value = glimkorr, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.
